item.title: Natore bus crash: Supervisor was driving, assistant slept in back seats
item.description:
Three passengers who survived a head-on collision between a bus and a sand-laden truck on the Natore-Pabna highway early Tuesday have said the bus was being driven by its supervisor while the driver and his assistant slept in the back seats, reports Bangla Tribune.
The RP Special Paribahan bus was being driven by supervisor Sohel Rana, 38, when the accident occurred in Natore, according to the survivors.
The crash occurred at around 4am in Bonpara, Baraigram upazila, killing 14 people, including Sohel Rana. At least 25 injured passengers were admitted to various hospitals with serious injuries, according to Bonpara Highway Police.
Sohel, a resident of Faradpur village in Godagari upazila of Rajshahi, had worked as a bus driver several years ago before becoming a supervisor around 2 years ago, according to his family members.
Ramzan Ali, 28, a passenger from Gomostapur upazila of Chapainawabganj, survived the crash but sustained injuries. He initially received treatment at Bonpara Patwari Hospital.
While traveling to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment, Ramzan said he had been sitting 2 seats behind the driver's seat.
“At around 3am, when the bus reached Ishwardi in Pabna, the driver got up from his seat. The supervisor then started driving the bus. The driver and his assistant closed the bus door and were sleeping in the back seats. About an hour later, the bus collided head-on with a sand-laden truck coming from the opposite direction,” he said.
Two other passengers, Yakub Ali and Abdus Salam, were also injured and received treatment at Bonpara Patwari Hospital. While undergoing treatment, they said the supervisor had been driving at reckless speed when the accident occurred, while the driver and helper were in the back seats.
The bus had departed from Barguna district town at around 7pm on Monday and stopped briefly in Ishwardi, Pabna. The supervisor began driving after the break, and the accident occurred some time later.
Sohel's body arrived at his village in Faradpur on Tuesday afternoon. Relatives mourned beside the body as villagers gathered to pay their respects.
Sohel's wife, Dolly Begum, said her husband had worked as a bus driver before becoming a supervisor around 2 years ago. Their family depended on his income, and she now faces an uncertain future with their children following his death.
Asked who was driving the bus at the time of the accident, Sub-Inspector Alamgir Hossain of Bonpara Highway Police Station said: “A case will be filed over the accident. An investigation will be conducted based on the case. Nothing can be confirmed about the matter before the investigation.”

item.title: Police rule out conspiracy in 34 pre-Puja incidents
item.description:
Police have said field-level verification of 34 incidents, including six involving idol damage, vandalism and clashes ahead of Durga Puja, found no evidence that they were deliberately orchestrated to undermine communal harmony, target religious minorities or disrupt the festival.
The statement, posted on Bangladesh Police’s official Facebook page, followed media reports citing complaints from Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad and the Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee that incidents of attacks, idol vandalism and theft at temples had occurred at 34 locations ahead of Durga Puja.
According to the police statement, verification identified different causes behind the incidents, including internal leadership disputes, theft by habitual or professional thieves, disagreements over the distribution of government funds, accidental damage and alleged vandalism by individuals described by local residents as mentally unstable.
Police highlighted six incidents in Narayanganj, Mymensingh, Pabna, Thakurgaon and Tangail to support its findings.
At around 2:30pm on October 16, the right hand of a demon figure accompanying an idol was slightly damaged while the idol was being unloaded from a vehicle for installation at Ramchandradi Madhya Monipara Sarbojanin Durga Puja Mandap in Araihazar, Narayanganj.
The temporary venue falls under Durga Puja Mandap Centre No 19. According to local accounts, the damage occurred accidentally due to carelessness during unloading.
Mandap president Mohan Bashi Das and general secretary Rajib Chandra Das confirmed the minor damage. A general diary (GD) was filed at Araihazar Police Station on October 17 (No 950).
At around 4pm on October 5, an argument broke out between the family of Pallab Das and their neighbour, Jibon Rishi, in Rishipara under Kotwali Police Station in Mymensingh.
The dispute reportedly concerned the picking of betel nuts.
At around 5:55pm, Jibon Rishi, his son Jayanta and his nephew Raymohan allegedly threw stones at the opposing family. Moyna Rani Das, 58, was injured, while parts of a Ganesh idol kept in front of a mandap for painting were damaged.
Mandap president Nripendra Das and general secretary Parimal Chandra Das said the incident stemmed from a longstanding dispute between the two families.
A GD was filed at Kotwali Police Station on October 5.
At around 11am on October 15, a woman reportedly tore the canopy of the Durga Puja pavilion at Radhanagar Sarbojanin Durga Mandir, near Mathurapur Government Primary School in the Bhayna area under Sujanagar Police Station in Pabna.
Police arrived after the temple committee reported the incident and took the woman into custody.
Residents said she had been staying in the area for four to five days.
Mandap president Samir Kumar Sarkar and general secretary Milon Kumar Sarkar reportedly said the woman was mentally unstable.
A GD was filed at Sujanagar Police Station on October 15 (No 847).
At around 9am on October 1, a dispute over idol installation broke out at Shri Shri Rasik Ray Jiou ISKCON Temple in Bhatgaon under Bhulli Police Station in Thakurgaon.
According to the report, around 70-80 members of the local Sanatan community entered the temple carrying sticks and assaulted four to five ISKCON members. They allegedly damaged property, forced the ISKCON members out and removed the ISKCON idol before installing their own.
Around 120 ISKCON members later arrived and attempted to intervene, triggering another physical confrontation.
Community leaders, administrative officials and political representatives subsequently held discussions to resolve the dispute. Following an agreement, the old idol was removed and replaced with a newly made one.
Shri Manoranjan Singha, president of the area's Puja Celebration Committee, said the incident primarily stemmed from a dispute between ISKCON and the local Sanatan community.
A GD was filed at Bhulli Police Station on October 1.
At around 11:30pm on October 2, an argument between groups associated with the neighbouring Krishna and Kali temples in Kashidangi Bairagipara under Baliadangi Police Station in Thakurgaon escalated into a physical altercation.
The dispute reportedly centred on a government grant of Tk100,000 allocated for temple development.
According to the police report, Krishna Temple president Kailash Mohanta, 45, and Kali Temple president Sudhir Mohanta, 48, had separately applied to the Thakurgaon District Council for financial assistance.
After learning that the grant had been allocated in the name of the Krishna Temple, both groups reportedly claimed that the funding had been sanctioned in response to their respective applications.
A GD was filed at Baliadangi Police Station on October 3.
At around 4:30pm on October 4, a dispute over the location of an idol installation led to a clash between supporters of two factions of the newly formed temporary committee of Purnachandra Nat Mandir in Nalkhi Para under Delduar Police Station in Tangail.
The committee had been discussing whether the idol for the 2026 Sarbojanin Durga Festival should be installed inside or outside the temple. An argument broke out between supporters of committee president Joyrath Pal and general secretary Dulal Chandra Pal before escalating into a physical altercation.
Police arrived and brought the situation under control. Later, supporters of the general secretary installed the idol inside the temple and hung a banner renaming the venue Sarbojanin Radha Gobinda Nat Mandir.
Shri Raghunath Basak, president of the Delduar Police Station Puja Celebration Committee, said the dispute was resolved through mediation by the local lawmaker.
Members of the local Hindu community agreed to prevent further disorder during the celebrations.
He added that the festival was being observed peacefully in a festive atmosphere.
A GD was filed at Delduar Police Station on October 4.
The Police Headquarters said police responded promptly to incidents involving attacks, idol vandalism and temple theft connected with the Durga Puja celebrations.
According to the statement, authorities took legal action, arrested suspects in various cases, recovered stolen property, helped resolve disputes between conflicting parties and maintained security at Puja venues.
The statement also said Durga Puja was being celebrated at more than 33,000 mandaps across Bangladesh in a festive atmosphere, with enthusiasm and public participation.
While reports citing complaints from the two Hindu organisations referred to incidents at 34 locations, the Police Headquarters presented the six cases above as examples of incidents whose circumstances were examined through field-level verification.
The police statement concluded that the verification findings did not substantiate allegations that these six incidents had been deliberately orchestrated to undermine communal harmony, persecute religious minorities or prevent the peaceful celebration of Durga Puja.

item.title: PM distributes Tk12C incentives to 38,970 Rajshahi sugarcane farmers
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday distributed Tk12 crore in government incentives to 38,970 sugarcane farmers in Rajshahi during a rally at the historic Madrasa Ground.
Tarique arrived at Shah Makhdum Airport in Rajshahi at 3pm and went directly to the rally, reaching the venue around 3:30pm.
Pressing a button on a laptop while seated on the stage, he launched the distribution of the funds. The money was transferred to the farmers’ bank accounts, and they received SMS notifications confirming the deposits.
During the first part of the rally, the prime minister announced the incentive distribution and later handed over symbolic cheques to 15 sugarcane farmers representing the country’s 15 sugar mills.
BNP lawmakers and party leaders addressed the gathering after the distribution programme.
This was Tarique Rahman’s first visit to Rajshahi since taking office as prime minister.
His late arrival prompted changes to the day’s initial itinerary. His scheduled visit to the Rajshahi Dharmasabha Temple in Ganakpara and lunch break at the circuit house were cancelled.
According to the original schedule, he was due to arrive in Rajshahi at around 1:15pm before visiting the temple and taking a break at the circuit house ahead of the rally.
Authorities and BNP leaders made extensive preparations across Rajshahi over the past several days ahead of the prime minister’s visit.
Roads along his route from the airport and elsewhere in the city were repaired, resurfaced and painted. Murals were painted on walls, drains were repaired, and hawkers were removed from several footpaths as part of efforts to clean up the route.
A large stage was built at the historic Madrasa Ground, and uneven sections of the field were levelled. BNP leaders and activists were present at the venue over the past several days to oversee preparations.
Although the rally was scheduled to begin in the afternoon, BNP leaders and activists started gathering in different parts of the city in the morning. Processions from various areas headed towards the venue, and the field was filled by around 2:30pm.
National and local BNP leaders began delivering speeches from the stage before the prime minister arrived.
Rajshahi-3 MP Advocate Shafiqul Haque Milon, Rajshahi-5 MP Professor Nazrul Islam, Rajshahi Development Authority Chairman Abul Kalam Azad Sweet, Divisional Commissioner Md Yusuf Ali, Rajshahi Range Deputy Inspector General Md Ashik Saeed, Rajshahi Metropolitan Police Commissioner Faizul Kabir, Deputy Commissioner Kazi Shahidul Islam and Superintendent of Police Md Mamun Or Rashid were among those who welcomed the prime minister at the airport.
After concluding his Rajshahi visit, Tarique was scheduled to leave for Chittagong aboard a military aircraft.
Earlier on Tuesday, he visited the Radha Gobinda Temple in Rangpur and addressed a roadside gathering there.
Thousands of people lined both sides of the Rajshahi-Naogaon highway from the morning, waiting for a glimpse of the prime minister.
Some carried national flags, while others held BNP flags. Men, women, children and party activists stood along the road, watching for his arrival.
Crowds gathered at several points along the highway to welcome Tarique, creating a festive atmosphere across the city.

item.title: Five Shariatpur traders among 14 killed in Natore road crash
item.description:
Five traders from Zajira upazila of Shariatpur were among the 14 people who were killed in a head-on collision between a bus and a sand-laden truck in Natore early Tuesday while they were heading towards Rajshahi to buy agricultural products.
The five deceased were as Jewel Madbar, 35, son of Zahir Uddin Madbar of Ramkrishnapur Madbarkandi village, Salal Mollah, 38, son of Jahan Uddin Mollah of Dubisayar Mollakandi, Sohag Shikder, 32, son of Yunus Shikder of Dubisayar Kazirhat, Samad Fakir, 45, a wholesale goods trader from Kazirhat and Shahin Bepari, 30, son of Razzak Bepari of Kathuria village under Palerchar Union.
They were heading to Taherpur wholesale market in Rajshahi to purchase maize, onions, garlic and various spices for their businesses.
Local sources said the five men had long been involved in trading agricultural products and other goods in Kazirhat and nearby markets in Zajira upazila.
They frequently travelled together to different markets to purchase merchandise.
News of the accident reached Jajira early Tuesday, triggering an outpouring of grief among the victims' relatives, friends and local residents.
Md Saleh Ahmed, Officer-in-Charge of Jajira Police Station said they learned about the accident through social media, but yet to receive an official communication from Natore district police or local highway authorities.
He said necessary legal procedures and cooperation regarding the handover of the bodies are underway.

item.title: President accepts Ishraque Hossain’s resignation
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has accepted the resignation of State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain.
The Cabinet Division issued a gazette notification in this regard on Tuesday.
The notification, signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani by order of the President, stated that the President had accepted the resignation of Ishraque Hossain, State Minister for Liberation War Affairs.
It also stated that the resignation would take effect immediately.
Earlier, on Monday, lawmaker Ishraque Hossain announced at a press conference that he was voluntarily resigning from the Cabinet. He clarified his position by outlining the circumstances surrounding an anti-drug drive in Gandaria in the capital and his carrying of a licensed firearm.
He announced his decision to step down from the post of state minister at the same press conference.
The gazette notification issued the following day formally made his resignation effective.

item.title: Jibanananda Das: A pioneer of surrealism in Bengali poetry
item.description:
I have a great fascination for the poetry of Jibanananda Das since I find in him the incarnation of deep poetic art that impresses any modern human being engaged in the act of creativity. His poetry artfully portrays the agonies of modern life, a deep feeling of meaninglessness and vacuity.
Most impressive are his poetic compositions enshrined in surrealism, which creates an aura of dreaminess beset with nebulous thoughts.
In fact, he is the pioneer of surrealistic poetry in the history of Bengali literature, and I daresay no later generation poets have ever surpassed him in this mastery of verbal art.
We may witness the role of dream in the process of his sublime creation.
The scenes in his poems, as if, emerge from a stream of unconscious associations.
In Aat Bochhor Ager Ekdin (One Day Eight Years Ago), the themes of death, memory, and loneliness are expressed through amorphous dictions.
The poem brings a scene of morgue in front of our eyes: “It was heard / he was taken to a morgue last night / in the darkness of spring / when the moon of the fifth day disappeared / he got a desire to die.”
External events are not presented merely as descriptions of incidents; instead, they become means of exploring existential anxiety.
In the poem Mrityur Agey (Before Death) the thought of death is met again: “Do we want to know it before death? Oh, we don’t know the face of grey death like wall, present around the bed of red desire.”
An atmosphere of gloominess recurs in his poems. We witness a sad incident of hunting a deer in the poem Kampey (In the Camp):
“Somewhere a deer is being hunted
The hunters have arrived in the forest
I as if get their smell
Lying on my bed here
I do not fall asleep
In the spring night.”
Jibanananda is most celebrated for his formidable imagery, which transport readers to an unfamiliar territory, wrapped in smog.
He stitches images as if making a panorama with pieces of clouds of different shapes, sizes and colors.
His depiction of nature invokes feelings of beauty, wonder, and mystery in the reader’s mind. In his poem Bodh (A Sense), the poet writes: “Inside my head / Not a dream—not love—some other awareness works!”
Here, the psychological experience falls outside conventional categories of feeling.
The mysterious awareness operates deep within the human mind, directing the individual towards an undefined world.
From a surrealist perspective, this awareness can be interpreted as an expression of the unconscious or the deeper psychological reality of human existence. As such, existential loneliness and the psychological crisis of modern humanity takes center stage.
Jibanananda is often praised as a poet of nature and patriotism. Even there, the familiar natural landscape unveils a mysterious world where we find a mix of reality and surreality.
We are amazed by his imaginative power. Rivers, paddy fields, birds, grass, mist, darkness, and stars touch a higher dimension.
In the poem Nirjan Swakkhor (Signature of Solitude), nature reveals itself with a profound vividness: “I am in green meadow and grass—the sky is lying in skies in blue form; yet can we yield colors of life, touching and stirring—a big wonder!”
We get a spectacular snapshot of morning environment in the poem Obosorer Gan (Song of Leisure):
“The morning sun has taken bed on paddy
Here in the late autumn like a lazy villager
The smell of grass in its bosom—
The fragrance of dew in its eyes
Rice ripens in fatigue getting a taste.”
In Rupasi Bangla (Beautiful Bengal), images of Bengali nature appear repeatedly. Although these elements belong to the familiar landscape of Bengal, Jibanananda’s imagination makes them beautifully surreal: “The bright starry sky in gesture / The grass of far-off land turns blue in the wind / Crickets and grasshoppers have slept / You are in the expansion of mango, neem and hijal trees. - Tumi “(You).”
The poet narrate the story of field with so appealing words:
The moon of meadow is looking
At my face, left and right
Barren land—straws, cracks in land
The water of dew
The moon of meadow curved like a sickle
Looking on
Countless times it has done so!
-“Mather Golpo (The Story of Meadow)”
In many poems of Jibananda, the difference between space and time is blurred, causing an effect of surrealism.
This may be observed in his famous poem Banalata Sen , where the poet describes himself as a traveler, not bound by temporal and spatial constraints.
During his extraordinary journey, he moves from the seas of Ceylon and Malaya to the historical worlds of Bimbisar and Ashok and finally to Vidarbha. Here, personal experience mingles with the vast historical tapestry.
The poet’s psychological journey gets interconnected with real geographical places and historical periods, as a manifestation of magic realism.
The poem opens with the celebrated line: “For thousands of years I have been walking the paths of the earth,” and ends with “Remains there only darkness and Banalata Sen in front of me.”
In another poem Poth Hanta (Walking), he narrates his experience of walking in remote corner of the world: “I have walked in Babylon along in deep night / I don’t know why even after so many busy years.” This is real, unreal and surreal.
Jibanananda Das occupies a unique position in the history of modern Bengali poetry.
Moving beyond the romantic tradition associated with Rabindranath Tagore, he introduced a new poetic style characterized by modernity, loneliness, nostalgia, sadness and love of nature.
In his poetry, the differences between reality and unreality, conscious and unconscious, past and present, and life and death often get neutralized. That is the aesthetic beauty of a great poet.
The more I read the poetry of Jibanananda, the more I am fascinated. And I think I will never get rid of this fascination in my life.
Dr Binoy Barman is a professor of English at Daffodil International University and the executive editor of the Journal of Society and Progress (JSP).

item.title: Dilip Agarwala put on one-day remand in money-laundering case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday placed Diamond World Managing Director Dilip Kumar Agarwala on one-day remand in a case filed over alleged laundering of Tk 678 crore.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Ariful Islam passed the order when Sub-Inspector Md Ashraful Hasan of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of police, also the investigating officer of the case, produced him before the court with a three-day remand prayer.
Earlier on Monday evening, detectives arrested Dilip Agarwala from the Banani area of the capital in the case filed by the CID on November 18 last year for allegedly laundering around Tk678 crore through smuggling gold and diamonds.
The Financial Crime Unit of CID filed the case against Dilip with Gulshan Police Station under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, said Jasim Uddin Khan, special superintendent of police (Media) of CID.
On September 29, 2024, the CID began an investigation against Dilip Agarwala after reviewing Diamond World Limited’s financial transactions, documents and bank accounts.
During the investigation, they found that the company procured smuggled gold and diamonds in the country.
According to the case statement, Dilip Agarwala had long been involved in money laundering and smuggling under the guise of gold and diamond business both at home and abroad as the proprietor of Diamond World and Diamond World Limited.
During the investigation, it was found that the company legally imported gold bars, jewellery, loose diamonds and other items worth Tk38,47,48,011.52 from abroad through letters of credit from September 6, 2006 to February 8, 2024.
During the same period, it also acquired gold and diamonds worth Tk6,78,19,14,014 from the local market through purchase and exchange.
However, the company failed to show valid documents to the CID regarding the source or suppliers of these materials.
Police earlier arrested Dilip Agarwala on September 3, 2024. On October 1, 2025, he was released on bail.

item.title: PM donates Tk 10 lakh to Dharmasabha Temple in Rajshahi
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited Dharmasabha Temple in the Miapara area of Rajshahi city and donated Tk 10 lakh on Tuesday afternoon after attending a public rally at Madrasa Ground.
At Dharmasabha, the prime minister held an exchange of views with leaders of the Puja Celebration Council from 5pm to 5:30pm. During the meeting, he handed over a cheque for Tk 10 lakh to Rajshahi Dharmasabha President Bishwanath Sarkar.
During the exchange of views, Tarique said people of all religions in Bangladesh were citizens of the country and that everyone's cooperation was needed to build a prosperous and developed Bangladesh.
He called on all citizens, regardless of religion or ethnicity, to come forward to help build the country. He also exchanged greetings with Hindu attendees and extended his Sharadiya greetings.
During the visit, leaders of the Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Welfare Front requested that the prime minister build a model temple in Rajshahi.
Security was tightened around Dharmasabha Temple ahead of the prime minister's visit and meeting with local representatives.
After visiting the temple, the prime minister left for Shah Makhdum Airport in Rajshahi at 5:37pm before departing for Chittagong.

item.title: A comprehensive guide to which savings certificate suits you best
item.description:
From managing household expenses, children’s education, and medical treatment to securing retirement life, people save according to their capacity to meet various future needs.
Some keep money in banks, others invest in land or alternative sectors.
Meanwhile, many look for investments where funds remain relatively safe and returns are generated at regular intervals.
Government savings certificates have long been a familiar option for such investors.
However, many people feel hesitant when buying savings certificates. Which option is more profitable: the 5-year Bangladesh Savings Certificate, the 3-Month Profit-Based Savings Certificate, the Family Savings Certificate, or the Pensioner Savings Certificate?
Which one pays out monthly? Who is eligible to buy which savings certificate? What kind of benefits can be expected from investing Tk1 lakh, Tk5 lakh, or Tk10 lakh?
These are common questions for many.
In reality, not every savings certificate suits everyone. Some are advantageous for earning regular income, others for long-term savings, and some are tailored to ensure the financial security of specific segments of the population during retirement.
Therefore, selecting a savings certificate based on one’s personal needs and eligibility—rather than just the profit rate—is the wisest approach.
Which Savings Certificate for Regular Income?
For individuals who need regular returns from their investments to run household expenses, the payout schedule is the most crucial factor.
In this regard, Family Savings Certificates and Pensioner Savings Certificates deserve special consideration. Both schemes offer the opportunity to receive monthly profits, subject to fulfilling designated conditions.
On the other hand, 3-Month Profit-Based Savings Certificates disburse profits every three months.
Additionally, the 5-year Bangladesh Savings Certificate can be suitable for those who wish to invest their funds for a comparatively longer duration.
5-Year Bangladesh Savings Certificate
Suppose a salaried employee has accumulated savings over several years and will not need those funds in the immediate future.
Instead, they want to set aside money for their child’s higher education, building a home, or other major future expenses. The 5-year Bangladesh Savings Certificate can be an alternative option for them.
This savings certificate allows investments under single or joint names. However, prescribed investment limits and cumulative limit regulations across other schemes must be observed. Upon maturity, the principal amount along with applicable profits is received.
The advantage here is that a specific target can be set for long-term savings. However, if there is a chance the funds might be needed before the 5-year term completes, the rules for early encashment should be thoroughly understood beforehand, as encashing before the designated maturity means forfeiting the full-term profit rate.
3-Month Profit-Based Savings Certificate
For those who do not want to spend their entire investment at once, and prefer receiving money in hand every few months rather than monthly, the 3-Month Profit-Based Savings Certificate is worth considering.
The tenure of this scheme is 3 years. Profits are distributed every three months according to established rules. Consequently, funds become available at specific intervals for rent, medical care, necessary family expenditures, or other costs.
Investors must keep in mind, however, that while profit payouts arrive periodically, the principal capital remains locked for an extended period. If the entire amount is required before the 3 years elapse, it is crucial to know the applicable profit rate and whether previously paid amounts will be adjusted.
Family Savings Certificate
The distinct feature of the Family Savings Certificate is that eligible women, individuals with physical disabilities, and Bangladeshi citizens aged 65 or older can invest in this scheme. It cannot be purchased under joint names.
Suppose a woman wants to earn a regular income from her personal savings. If she meets the eligibility criteria to buy a Family Savings Certificate, this scheme could be an option for her. Similarly, senior citizens or eligible individuals with physical disabilities can also consider this benefit.
Family Savings Certificates offer monthly profit payouts, which can help cover regular household costs or personal needs. Before purchasing, however, age criteria, eligibility, maximum investment limits, and applicable documentation requirements must be verified.
Pensioner Savings Certificate
Upon retirement from employment, many individuals receive a lump-sum gratuity or provident fund payout. At this stage of life, even though regular salaries stop, household, medical, and daily expenses continue. Consequently, figuring out how to utilize the lump-sum money to maintain financial security over a long period becomes a major question.
The Pensioner Savings Certificate serves as an option in this scenario. However, only retired employees of specific government, semi-government, and autonomous institutions, retired judges, retired members of the armed forces, and eligible family pension beneficiaries according to regulations are permitted to invest in this scheme.
It provides the opportunity to receive monthly profits, making it possible to arrange a regular income stream from retirement funds. Nonetheless, simply being retired does not automatically qualify anyone to purchase this certificate; eligibility and conditions concerning the source of funds must be satisfied.
What to calculate when investing Tk10 lakh
Many people want to know how much profit they will earn by investing Tk10 lakh before purchasing a savings certificate. In such cases, one must first check which scheme is being chosen and which tier's rate applies to that amount.
For instance, for an investment of Tk10 lakh, the rate designated for investments exceeding ৳7.5 lakh may apply.
Consequently, the entire Tk10 lakh cannot be calculated using the higher profit rate meant exclusively for the first Tk7.5 lakh.
Simultaneously, the profit-payout intervals differ across the four savings certificates. Family and Pensioner Savings Certificates yield monthly profits, the 3-Month Profit-Based scheme delivers funds every three months, and the 5-year Bangladesh Savings Certificate pays out according to its term and encashment regulations.
Key factors to consider before buying savings certificates
Several aspects must be verified prior to investing in savings certificates.
First, check whether you meet the eligibility criteria for the respective scheme.
Second, verify the investment limits for single or joint names.
Third, determine the applicable withholding tax rate on profits.
Fourth, understand the financial impact of early encashment before maturity.
Furthermore, applications must accurately provide National Identity Cards, bank account details, nominee information, and income tax documents where applicable.
Incorrect bank account numbers can cause delays in receiving principal or profit payments.
The primary appeal of savings certificates lies in relatively safe investment opportunities and structured profit payouts.
However, there is no single answer as to which savings certificate is the "best." For someone needing extra monthly income, Family or Pensioner Savings Certificates may be more suitable.
Profit rates across different savings certificates
According to government decisions, two tiers have been established for savings certificate investors.
The first tier applies to investors with investments under Tk7.50 lakh, while the second tier applies to those with investments exceeding Tk7.50 lakh.
Based on the profit rates effective from July to December 2026, first-tier investors in 5-year Bangladesh Savings Certificates who encash before maturity will receive profits at 9.74% for the first year, 10.21% for the second year, 10.72% for the third year, 11.26% for the fourth year, and 11.83% for the fifth year.
On the other hand, second-tier investors in 5-year Bangladesh Savings Certificates encashing prior to maturity will receive profits at 9.72% for the first year, 10.19% for the second year, 10.70% for the third year, 11.23% for the fourth year, and 11.80% for the fifth year.
3-Month Profit-Based Savings Certificates
First-tier investors in 3-Month Profit-Based Savings Certificates who encash before maturity will receive profits at 10.65% for the first year, 11.22% for the second year, and 11.82% for the third year.
Conversely, second-tier investors encashing prior to maturity will receive profits at 10.60% for the first year, 11.16% for the second year, and 11.77% for the third year.
Pensioner Savings Certificates
First-tier investors in Pensioner Savings Certificates encashing before maturity will receive profits at 9.84% for the first year, 10.32% for the second year, 10.84% for the third year, 11.39% for the fourth year, and 11.98% for the fifth year.
Second-tier investors encashing prior to maturity will receive profits at 9.72% for the first year, 10.19% for the second year, 10.84% for the third year, 11.39% for the fourth year, and 11.98% for the fifth year.
Family Savings Certificates
First-tier investors in Family Savings Certificates encashing before maturity will receive profits at 9.81% for the first year, 10.29% for the second year, 10.80% for the third year, 11.35% for the fourth year, and 11.93% for the fifth year.
Meanwhile, second-tier investors encashing prior to maturity will receive profits at 9.72% for the first year, 10.19% for the second year, 10.70% for the third year, 11.23% for the fourth year, and 11.80% for the fifth year.
Post Office Fixed Deposits
First-tier investors in Post Office Fixed Deposits encashing before maturity will receive profits at 10.65% for the first year, 11.22% for the second year, and 11.82% for the third year.
On the other side, second-tier investors encashing prior to maturity will receive profits at 10.60% for the first year, 11.16% for the second year, and 11.77% for the third year.

item.title: BSEC grants time to 12 capital market entities to meet deficits
item.description:
The Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC), the capital market regulator, has decided to allow operations and grant time to clear deficits for 12 capital market subsidiary companies under 9 financial institutions that are currently undergoing Bangladesh Bank's license cancellation process.
This decision was made during a commission meeting of BSEC on Monday.
Following the meeting, the information was shared in a press release signed by BSEC executive director and spokesperson Md Abul Kalam.
According to the BSEC decision, several stockbrokers and merchant banks have been given until April 30, 2027.
Meanwhile, FAS Capital Management Limited has been granted until December 31, 2026, to resolve non-asset-related deficits and ensure compliance with necessary regulations.
The press release stated that several institutions, including four stockbrokers and two merchant banks, have compliance deficits under securities laws and regulations.
A stipulated time frame has been provided to ensure compliance with relevant regulations and registration certificate conditions for these entities.
The four stockbrokers named on the list are Premier Leasing Securities Limited, International Leasing Securities Limited, Fareast Stocks & Bonds Limited, and PFI Securities Limited.
The two merchant banks included under the decision are IL Capital Limited and GSP Investment Limited.
Additionally, Prime Finance Asset Management Company Limited has also been brought under this ruling.
On the other hand, the Commission has decided to keep operations active and address certain asset-related matters for two stockbrokers—Premier Leasing Securities Broking Limited and Aviva Equity Management Limited—as well as two merchant banks—PLFS Investments Limited and Prime Finance Capital Management Limited.
The Commission decided to maintain their non-asset and non-asset-related activities while also making decisions regarding certain valuations and asset matters.
Furthermore, FAS Capital Management Limited has been given a deadline of December 31, 2026, to clear non-asset-related deficits and achieve full regulatory compliance.
This decision by the BSEC regarding capital market-related entities operating under financial institutions undergoing license cancellation by Bangladesh Bank is viewed as a crucial step toward maintaining operations and regulatory compliance.

item.title: Bangladeshis spend 4x more abroad on cards than foreigners domestically
item.description:
Bangladeshis are spending nearly four times as much abroad using cards compared to what foreign nationals spend using cards within Bangladesh.
In August, spending by Bangladeshis abroad via cards reached approximately Tk987 crore.
In contrast, foreigners spent nearly Tk249 crore in Bangladesh using their cards.
This wide gap between outward and inward expenditure highlights a significant international presence in the country's card-based transactions.
According to Bangladesh Bank data, Bangladeshis spent around Tk985 crore abroad via cards in July, which slightly increased to Tk987 crore in August.
On the other hand, foreign nationals' card spending within Bangladesh grew by 6.27% in one month, rising from Tk234 crore to nearly Tk249 crore.
In August, spending by Bangladeshis via credit cards abroad stood at Tk504.60 crore.
Debit cards accounted for Tk422.10 crore, and prepaid cards accounted for Tk60.10 crore.
Domestic credit card usage drops
While overseas spending rose, domestic credit card transactions inside the country dropped.
Spending dropped by 5.44%, falling from Tk4,324.80 crore in July to Tk4,089.30 crore in August.
Department stores accounted for 48.14% of total domestic credit card spending, followed by retail outlets (12.67%), utility bill payments (10.80%), and medicine/pharmacies (6.94%).
Cash withdrawals accounted for 6.43%. However, transactions at retail outlets increased from Tk487.90 crore to Tk518.30 crore.
Spending on utility bills, medicine, clothing, and transportation also saw an increase.
At the end of September 2021, the country had 24.225 million debit cards, 1.763 million credit cards, and 1.027 million prepaid cards.
By August 2026, those numbers expanded to 40.087 million debit cards, 2.805 million credit cards, and 9.271 million prepaid cards.
Over five years, the total number of cards grew by 96%, while overall transaction volume surged by 103%. Prepaid cards experienced the fastest growth.
At the end of August, the total approved credit limit against credit cards stood at Tk43,108 crore, with outstanding loans amounting to Tk14,482 crore.
Arief Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson of Bangladesh Bank, told Dhaka Tribune that the central bank is taking various initiatives to discourage cash transactions and promote digital payments, including efforts to expand transactions via Bangla QR alongside traditional payment cards.

item.title: Minister: Religion should not be used to create political divisions
item.description:
Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology and Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam has said religion should not be used to create political divisions, urging people of all faiths to work together to advance Bangladesh.
“Everyone has their own religion, but the country belongs to all of us,” he said while attending a programme in Dhanbari of Tangail on Tuesday.
The minister distributed cash assistance from his personal fund among 36 Durga Puja mandaps and saris from the prime minister’s relief and welfare fund among members of the Hindu community.
He called for celebrating all religious festivals peacefully to strengthen communal harmony and urged people to refrain from creating divisions through politics. Supporting members of the Hindu community in times of need, he added, was a shared responsibility.
The programme was chaired by Dhanbari upazila BNP President Principal MA Azizur Rahman. Local BNP leaders, Hindu community representatives and other dignitaries attended.
Earlier, the minister inaugurated a newly built visitor room at Madhupur Upazila Parishad and planted a sapling at Dhanbari Upazila Parishad as part of a nationwide programme to plant 25 crore trees.

item.title: Keya Group lays off 739 more workers in Gazipur
item.description:
Keya Group has laid off 739 more workers and employees from its four factories in Konabari of Gazipur.
A notice announcing the decision was posted at the factories’ main gate around 10:30 pm on Monday. Workers gathered outside the factory on Tuesday morning to check the lists of those affected.
The factories are Keya Group’s Knit Composite Division, Spinning Division, Cotton Division, and Keya Yarn Mills Ltd.
According to the notice, the factories have been under lay-off since June 6 due to banking complications and unpaid gas bills, with the period extended several times.
The notice, signed by the company’s managing director and chairman, cited gas disconnection, banking complications, and excess manpower as reasons for cutting production and administrative costs. Some positions across different sections and divisions have been abolished.
The layoffs took effect yesterday under Section 20 of Bangladesh Labor Act, 2006. The company said workers would receive their lawful dues.
Ashrafuzzaman, organising secretary of the central committee of Jatiya Garments Sramik Jote, condemned the layoffs, saying 739 workers at Keya Knit Composite had been dismissed through a single notice following five rounds of lay-offs. He demanded payment of outstanding dues, lawful benefits, and compensation.
A company official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said employees whose jobs remained intact would continue under the lay-off arrangements and receive benefits as required by law. Skilled workers who had been laid off would get priority in future recruitment under Section 21 of the Labor Act, the official added.
Keya Group Human Resources Manager Sabina Yasmin said all dues would be paid in accordance with labor laws.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amzad Hossain confirmed the layoffs, adding that police had been deployed at the factory gate to maintain law and order.

item.title: Moulvibazar village preserves 300-year-old red Durga tradition
item.description:
While Goddess Durga is traditionally depicted in golden or fair hues, a centuries-old tradition in Panchgaon village of Rajnagar upazila, Moulvibazar, sees the goddess worshipped in a distinctive red complexion.
For more than 300 years, the unique tradition has drawn thousands of devotees and visitors from across Bangladesh and abroad during Durga Puja, turning the village into a major gathering place for worshippers eager to witness the rare custom and seek the goddess’s blessings.
According to local folklore, the tradition was introduced nearly three centuries ago by Sarbananda Das, a spiritual practitioner who lived in Assam’s Sivasagar for work.
Legend has it that while performing worship at the Kamakhya Temple in Assam, Das witnessed a miraculous event. During the rituals, the complexion of a young girl reportedly turned crimson. Believing that the goddess herself had appeared before him, Das prayed for her to visit his birthplace, Panchgaon, every year during Durga Puja.
According to local belief, the goddess instructed him that her idol in Panchgaon must be worshipped in red. Since then, the distinctive tradition has been preserved through successive generations, making the red-hued idol the defining feature of the village’s Durga Puja celebrations.
Every year, Panchgaon comes alive during the festival as thousands of devotees from different parts of Bangladesh and abroad gather at the temple to see the red Durga idol and offer prayers.
Alongside the religious rituals, a large fair is held on the temple premises, drawing visitors from different communities and adding to the festive atmosphere.
Sumanta Das, president of the Panchgaon Union Parishad Puja Celebration Committee, said the temple had attracted devotees for more than three centuries and that the tradition had gained recognition beyond Bangladesh.
“This is not merely a religious ceremony; it is a symbol of our longstanding heritage and the deep faith of devotees. It is our responsibility to preserve this tradition, which has continued for generations,” he said.
Local authorities have taken measures to ensure peaceful celebrations. Enamul Haque Chowdhury, officer-in-charge of Rajnagar police station, said police were working to maintain law and order at puja mandaps across the upazila.
He expressed hope that the celebrations would conclude peacefully in a festive atmosphere.
Beyond its religious significance, Panchgaon is associated with important historical events. The village bears memories of Bangladesh’s 1971 Liberation War and is linked to the legacy of Leela Nag, a prominent revolutionary figure of the Indian subcontinent.
Its centuries-old religious tradition, historical connections and deep-rooted local beliefs have given Panchgaon a distinctive identity.
For local residents, the worship of the red-hued Durga is more than a religious festival. It is an enduring symbol of the region’s history, culture and heritage.

item.title: Tk9.33cr drain project stalled for six months, commuters suffer in Chapainawabganj
item.description:
Construction of a 2.1km drain in Shibganj municipality of Chapainawabganj has remained stalled for six months due to objections from local residents, leaving thousands of commuters, students and traders suffering.
The Tk9.33 crore project, stretching from Academy Mor to Debinagar, has been held up, with rainwater accumulating in road potholes, disrupting traffic and business activities.
The road serves several important institutions, including a police station, hospital, government high school and college, upazila parishad, sub-registry office, Sonali Bank branch, insurance offices, an orphanage, madrasa and mosques. Thousands of people use the route every day.
Excavated sections along the roadside have made movement hazardous. The prolonged suspension of work has also sparked frustration among residents, who are demanding the project's early completion.
According to municipal sources, construction began around two years ago under the Inclusive Urban Governance and Infrastructure Improvement Project (IUGIIP) to address waterlogging. Of the planned 2.1km drain, around 300 metres remain unfinished.
The municipality said work had been suspended for six months after three local residents obstructed excavation on municipal land.
Contractor Jahangir Alam said the project had been nearing completion when the objections halted progress.
“Construction cannot proceed because three local residents are obstructing excavation on the land designated by the municipality. The remaining work can be completed quickly if the municipal authorities take the necessary steps,” he said.
Two residents, Mahbub and Alim, named as having obstructed the work, could not be reached for comment.
Another resident, Saidul Islam, said four to five feet of municipal land fell within his homestead. He said they had objected to the work because they wanted the drain shifted slightly away from the boundary wall to protect their houses.
Shibganj Municipality Administrator and Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mazharul Islam said parts of several houses and a mosque fell within the land designated for drain construction.
He said the authorities would hold discussions with residents to resolve the dispute and complete the remaining work as soon as possible.
However, with construction still stalled on the busy road, commuters and businesses continue to bear the brunt, with no clear timeline for an end to their suffering.

item.title: Maddison sparkles as Spurs end EPL winless run London
item.description:
James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham's starting line-up on Monday as Roberto De Zerbi's men beat Coventry 3-1 to claim their first Premier League win of the season.
On a feel-good night in London, Maddison marked his first start in 17 months with a spectacular early goal while Dejan Kulusevski returned to the matchday squad after missing the whole of last season.
Jack Rudoni levelled early in the second half but the home side were back in front just before the hour mark when Omar Marmoush lashed home his first goal for the club and substitute Ben Davies made the points safe in added time.
"I just wanted to play well, I just wanted to show my qualities and show what I bring to the team and what the team's missed in the last 18 months or whatever it is from my last start," Maddison told Sky Sports.
"So the gaffer asked me to play and he wanted to enjoy watching me from the side, so hopefully I did that."
The Spurs playmaker said he believed he could help propel his team up the table as they seek to avoid the indignity of last season, when they narrowly escaped relegation.
"I'm 29, I've still got plenty of years left, and I have a lot of self-belief, and I know that I have quality that can really help us in this league," he added.
Winless Spurs Spurs came into the match rock bottom of the Premier League and with the unwanted record of being the only team in England's top six divisions without a league win this season despite a huge summer outlay.
De Zerbi had taken his squad to Marbella in southern Spain for some warm-weather training in a bid to kickstart their season and it paid off against Frank Lampard's competitive Coventry side.
Maddison, who ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee, put his side ahead in the 14th minute after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right.
Lurking just outside the penalty area, he received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans.
Maddison came close to doubling Spurs' lead after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide.
Newly promoted Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range.
Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni's effort hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him again and he drove home.
Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when Manchester City loanee Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing a powerful shot from distance.
Kulusevski, whose career was interrupted by a knee injury in May 2025, was brought off the substitutes' bench in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans.
Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe in the dying minutes, poking home from the edge of the penalty area.
The win lifts Spurs up to 16th in the table, buying De Zerbi much-needed breathing space.

item.title: Bayern set for Arsenal test without red-hot Olise
item.description:
Champions League hopefuls Bayern Munich are set for an early test of their title credentials when they host English champions Arsenal on Wednesday without in-form winger Michael Olise.
The London-born Olise, who started in Arsenal's junior system, is suspended after picking up two yellow cards inside a minute in Bayern's 3-3 draw with Viking last week.
After seeing a first yellow for a foul, a clearly frustrated Olise responded to some verbal provocation from Viking captain Zlatko Tripic by throwing the ball at his head to be sent off for the first time in his career.
After being thrust into Ballon d'Or contention due to last season's stellar showing, the former Crystal Palace winger has continued his excellent form this campaign.
Olise has nine goals and five assists from 10 games in all competitions for Bayern.
With Jamal Musiala struggling with injury and illness and both Serge Gnabry and Lennart Karl well off their best form, Olise and the ever-reliable Harry Kane have shouldered Bayern's attacking burden so far this season.
The England captain has nine goals and six assists in 10 games. With Bayern 2-0 down away at Viking last week, Kane almost single-handedly engineered a comeback, scoring twice and setting up another.
Speaking after Bayern's ruthless 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, Kane said Bayern would miss Olise but called on the rest of their star-studded squad to step up.
"Missing one of your biggest players, you're going to feel it for sure, but that's where other people have to step up and show they can take their opportunity," Kane said.
"We talk about the squad a lot, we talk about being ready for your moment and whoever plays will have to be ready."
One of the many positives to come out of Saturday's thumping win over Leipzig was the performance of Luis Diaz.
The 29-year-old had cut a frustrated figure after a poor start to the season but scored three goals and set up another in one of his best performances since moving from Liverpool in 2025.
'ONE OF THE BEST'
Despite swapping north London for the Bavarian capital back in 2023, former Tottenham captain Kane has seen plenty of Arsenal since joining Bayern.
Bayern faced the Gunners in two quarterfinal legs in 2023-24, progressing by just a goal, but were outclassed in a 3-1 defeat in the league phase of last year's competition.
With domestic and international matches coming thick and fast, Kane has not had time to exchange pleasantries with any of his Gunners rivals.
"I spoke to them a bit in the international break previously and we knew the game was coming up, but I think we're all too busy right now to text each other, with a game every three days," he explained.
Saturday's thrashing of Leipzig once again showed the perennial German champions are a cut above their domestic rivals and Kane said Bayern were relishing a chance to take on Mikel Arteta's side.
Still smarting from last year's painful loss on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal have started strongly, winning 10 of 11 games in all competitions.
"It's a big game and we're playing against one of the best teams in Europe, you have to always enjoy these occasions," Kane said.
"We're testing ourselves against one of the best, we're here at home, the energy, the fans, it's going to be a special night."

item.title: Koko's legacy to be honoured thru Summer Athletics Competition
item.description:
The Bangladesh Athletics Federation (BAF) has named its 18th National Summer Athletics Competition after Arafat Rahman Koko, aiming to highlight his contribution as a sports organiser and inspire the younger generation to follow his legacy.
The three-day Koko 18th National Summer Athletics Competition 2026 will begin on October 23 at the National Stadium in the capital, with President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, is expected to grace the opening ceremony as the chief guest.
The BAF joint secretary Monzur Morshed told BSS that the initiative has been taken to recognise Koko's role in sports administration, particularly his contributions to the development of cricket in Bangladesh, and to ensure that the younger generation remains aware of his work.
"We want the present generation to know about Koko's contributions and remember him for his achievements as a sports organiser. We want to draw inspiration from his work to take athletics forward in Bangladesh," he said.
State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque will attend the inaugural ceremony as a special guest, while Water Resources Minister Water Resources Minister Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee is expected to attend as the chief guest on October 24.
The federation is also seeking the consent of State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir to attend the closing ceremony on October 25 as the chief guest.
The competition will feature 40 events- 22 for men and 18 for women-with around 800 athletes expected to participate from all 64 districts, different divisions and various services teams, including the Bangladesh Army, Bangladesh Navy, Bangladesh Air Force, Bangladesh Ansar, Border Guard Bangladesh and Bangladesh police.
Athletes from private universities and physical education colleges are also expected to compete in the mega tournament.
The competition men's event are 100m sprint, 200m sprint, 400m splint, 800m run, 1500m run, 3,000m steeplechase, 5000m run, 10,000m run, 110m hurdles, 400m hurdles, 20km walk, marathon, 4x100 m relay, 4x400m relay, long jump, high jump, triple jump, pole volt, shot-put, discus throw, javelin throw and hammer throw while the women's event are 100m sprint, 200m sprint, 400m sprint, 800m sprint, 1500m sprint, 300m sprint, 500m sprint, 10,00m sprint, 100m hurdles, 4x400m relay, long jump, high jump, triple shot-put, discus throw and javelin throw.
The BAF joint secretary hopes the competition would help generate greater public interest in athletics, a sport it considers fundamental to international multi-sport events but one that remains underrepresented in Bangladesh.
"Athletics is the foundation of sports, yet our representation in major international competitions remains limited. We want to build a stronger athletics contingent for the Olympics, Asian Games and other international events," Morshed said further.
The federation joint secretary expressed optimism about the sport's future, citing the commitment of its president, other federation officials and sponsors to athletics development.
The prize money for the top three finishers-Taka 6,000 for gold-, Taka 4,000 for silver- and Taka 3,000 for bronze-winners. Meanwhile competition sponsor has announced an exploit e-bike motorcycle for the competition's best athlete, while the federation decided to give additional rewards of Taka 20,000 for athlete who set new national record.
The BAF hopes sustained sponsorship and wider public participation will help strengthen athletics and improve Bangladesh's performance on the international stage.

item.title: Alberta separatists lose vote on leaving Canada
item.description:
Canada’s province of Alberta rejected a plan to hold a binding independence referendum, results showed Tuesday, a win for unity as the country faces worsening ties with the United States.
Public broadcaster CBC and leading private network CTV projected a clear win for the federalist side, with official results showing more than 76 percent support for Alberta remaining in Canada with nearly 45% of ballots counted.
Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomed the result and said Albertans had made a “clear choice” in favor of unity.
“They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other,” he said in a statement on X.
Carney, who grew up in Alberta, urged the province to reject separatism and argued that Canada needed stability as it confronted US President Donald Trump’s trade war and annexation threats.
A sombre mood took over the restaurant in the provincial capital Edmonton where a leading separatist group watched the returns.
Jeffrey Rath, a top leader of the separatist Alberta Prosperity Project, told reporters his push for independence will “absolutely” continue, despite the result from Monday’s vote.
“As far as I’m concerned we’ve already won. We’ve created a massive movement in this province,” Rath said.
“We’ve been educating Albertans on the benefits of independence and we’re continuing to move forward.”
Separatist supporter Roger Hodkinson, an 82-year-old retired doctor, told AFP “this movement is not going to stop.”
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, a conservative who opposed independence, praised the “widespread support for remaining in Canada” on Tuesday.
Smith, who called the referendum, said a win for the federalists would settle the secession issue, which has divided the province.
Thomas Lukaszuk, who leads the pro-unity group Forever Canadian, said it was “amazing to see the enthusiasm and resolve among Canadians.”
Alberta has the world’s fourth-largest proven oil reserves, and much of the separatist momentum has been driven by anger over oil industry management.
Smith blamed Carney’s predecessor Justin Trudeau for igniting the separatist fire, accusing him of trying to crush oil production to advance his pro-climate agenda.
Alberta’s independence push has also drawn sustained interest from Trump allies.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Alberta a “natural partner” for the United States. Elon Musk, the world’s richest person and a top Trump supporter, posted on X this month that Alberta “should separate.”
Rath of the Alberta Prosperity Project also held meetings at the US State Department, while separatists received advice from Republican political operatives.
Carney has worked to improve relations between the province and Ottawa since taking office last year.
He has partnered with Smith on advancing a new pipeline to export more Alberta bitumen overseas, a project considered a nonstarter during Trudeau’s tenure.
Alberta Prosperity Project leader Mitch Sylvestre told AFP earlier Monday that Carney had “threatened” the province in the closing days of the campaign.
Carney’s message was “voting against Canada is dangerous,” Sylvestre said, calling that “very unreasonable.”
Haley Erdegard, a 44-year-old who voted in Edmonton, voiced discomfort with the idea advanced by some separatists that Alberta is forced to share too much of its oil revenue with the rest of Canada.
“I think we probably need to put some more work towards cooperation before making rash decisions about trying to start our own country,” she told AFP.

item.title: France pledges new curfews as PM seeks to regain control after unrest
item.description:
France will impose new curfews where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, as authorities sought to restore order after weekend demonstrations degenerated into riots.
The eurozone’s second-largest economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst street violence in recent years, just six months before the country elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.
Images of clashes and public buildings set on fire or vandalized circulated around the world, prompting several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.
Accused of failing to anticipate and contain the street violence, the government has pledged to restore order, and had announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities on Monday.
The targeted measures had “helped keep the night calm,” Lecornu said.
Macron, currently on a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, has acknowledged shortcomings in the handling of the protests.
The presidency said Macron had secured the delivery of an additional 200,000 tons of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain during the tour.
Lecornu said that new curfews would be decided “where the situation requires it.”
“Targeted curfews have contributed to calm overnight,” he wrote on X.
The government scheduled another series of emergency meetings on Tuesday, including talks involving representatives of major social media platforms.
Under pressure, Lecornu will convene political parties for a meeting on Thursday, a member of his team said. He will also meet with trade unions on Wednesday.
The government has come under criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a “wake-up call” that exposed a “profound crisis” of authority.
Police confirmed the night had passed without major incidents across France.
Several cities, including Paris, the southwestern city of Bordeaux and Nice on the French Riviera, introduced partial curfews on Monday in response to urban unrest that followed weeks of student demonstrations over poor learning conditions in high schools.
While some restrictions, such as those in Paris, initially applied only for the night from Monday to Tuesday, others, particularly in Bordeaux and Nice, were set to remain in force for several days.
During the night, a helicopter flew over the French capital’s Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a powerful searchlight across the square to monitor compliance with the curfew.
In Lyon, despite a ban on demonstrations, around 500 people gathered on Monday evening outside the tourism office that was set on fire, to show support for shopkeepers affected by looting, according to organizers.
The word “LYON” had been spelled out on the ground with candles.
A banner hung on a fence nearby read “Anti-Rioters Lyon” and “Doucet Resign,” referring to Green mayor Gregory Doucet, an AFP journalist said.
Nationwide, more than 2,500 people have been taken into police custody since the weekend, and 67 people had been jailed.
Some demonstrators were seriously injured. In the eastern city of Mulhouse, a 17-year-old girl lost an eye. In Saint-Etienne, a 17-year-old boy had his hand blown off by a grenade.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered to resign on Sunday, saying police “had lost control” during the unrest. Macron rejected his resignation.
Finance Minister Roland Lescure has pledged support measures for shopkeepers and craftspeople.
Patrick Martin, the head of France’s Medef business lobby group, on Tuesday accused the state of having “failed” during the urban unrest that hit at least 3,000 businesses, according to preliminary estimates.
Donald Trump has seized on the unrest in France to amplify his anti-immigration and anti-Islam rhetoric, as the upcoming midterm elections force his Republican party to face strong headwinds.
“What’s happening in France has to do with immigration, not schools, not anything,” Trump told reporters in Washington.
“It’s immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders.”

item.title: Rajshahi Dharmasabha preserves city's print history ahead of PM visit
item.description:
Rajshahi's early newspaper publishing and printing history is drawing renewed attention ahead of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's scheduled visit to the city's 19th-century Rajshahi Dharmasabha on Tuesday during Sharadiya Durga Puja.
The historic institution is associated with the city's first newspaper and printing press.
The Dharmasabha's history is inseparable from Hindu Ranjika, regarded as Rajshahi's first newspaper, and Tamoghna Yantralaya, recognized as the city's first printing press. Local historians say preserving the institution's history is essential to passing on Rajshahi's heritage to younger generations.
Hindu Ranjika began publication in 1865, marking a significant chapter in Rajshahi's newspaper history. Its first editor was Srinath Singh Roy.
Initially published monthly, the newspaper became a weekly in 1868, 3 years after its launch. Its publication opened a new avenue for written news and public opinion in Rajshahi.
The establishment of the Rajshahi Dharmasabha was linked to the social and cultural conditions of the second half of the 19th century, particularly the 1860s. Promoting the philosophy, ideals and culture of Sanatan Dharma was one of its principal objectives.
People familiar with the institution say it also contributed to the spread of education, cultural activities and social awareness within Hindu society.
During this period, a new intellectual environment was emerging across Bengal, including Rajshahi, around education, social reform, religious debates and newspaper publishing. The spread of printing presses and periodicals created greater opportunities for public expression, the exchange of ideas and social communication.
Local historians believe a similar environment developed around the Rajshahi Dharmasabha. Beyond its role as a religious institution, it became a center of contemporary thought and cultural activity.
According to local elders, the institution was associated not only with religious and social activities but also with the political activities of the progressive society of the time.
In 1872, Harnath Roy Chowdhury, the zamindar of Dublahati, received the title of Raja from the British government. He provided the Dharmasabha with a printing machine and premises.
The machine was the first printing press in Rajshahi and was installed primarily to facilitate the publication of Hindu Ranjika and other religious books.
Raja Harnath Roy Chowdhury of Dublahati played an important role in establishing Tamoghna Yantralaya, recognized as Rajshahi's first printing press. Local historians say the press was established with his financial assistance.
In the 19th century, establishing a printing press was more than a business venture. Such institutions provided infrastructure for the production and circulation of knowledge and information through newspapers, books and other printed materials.
Tamoghna Yantralaya therefore holds a significant place in Rajshahi's history of printing and publishing.
Ranjit Kumar Saha, a member of the Rajshahi Dharmasabha and principal of Varendra College, said the occupying forces caused extensive damage to the institution during the Liberation War.
He said its historical significance could not be fully understood if it were viewed merely as a religious structure, as it also preserves memories of Rajshahi's social and cultural development.
Saha said proper recognition and preservation were needed to bring this history to younger generations.
Kalpana Roy, who worked at the printing press in the 1980s and served as manager of Tamoghna Yantralaya, also has memories of an important period in the early history of Rajshahi's printing industry.
She said poor Hindu students from the region were able to stay at the Dharmasabha almost free of charge. A printing machine was donated to help cover the institution's expenses.
Roy described the machine as expensive but said its importance gradually declined with the arrival of offset printing.
The history of the Rajshahi Dharmasabha has come into renewed focus ahead of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's scheduled visit to inspect the historic institution in Rajshahi on the occasion of Sharadiya Durga Puja.
Local residents believe the visit offers an opportunity to highlight the site's historical importance, particularly its role in the development of newspaper publishing, printing and cultural activities in the city.
They hope the visit will go beyond a formal inspection and lead to effective measures to preserve the Dharmasabha's history and architectural heritage.
In particular, they have called for the old temple at the site to be rebuilt according to its original design, citing its archaeological and historical significance.
